question.problem: A teacher is grading a math test. Typically, $90%$ of students pass the test. What is the probability that the teacher starts grading the first test with a passing grade after having already graded more than $3$ tests?
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of graded tests until a passing test starts to be graded. Since the chance of passing the test is $90%,$ the number of graded tests until starting to grade the first passing one can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=90%=\frac{90}{100}=0.9.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.9).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.9)^{x-1}(0.9) \\  & =(0.1)^{x-1}(0.9)\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X>3),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>3)=1-P(X\le 3)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(0.1)^{1-1}(0.9)+(0.1)^{2-1}(0.9)+(0.1)^{3-1}(0.9) \\  & =(0.9)+(0.1)(0.9)+(0.1)^{2}(0.9) \\  & =[1+0.1+(0.1)^{2}](0.9) \\  & =0.999.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the first passing test will begin being graded after grading $3$ tests is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & =1-P(X\le 3) \\  & =1-0.999 \\  & =0.001.\end{aligned}
$$
